precepts.text: Ye that love the Lord, hate evil. In order for the Lord to deliver us out of the hands of the wicked, we must train ourselves to hate evil. As long as you watch pornography, you don't hate evil. You might say it on the street, but at home you don't hate evil.
precepts.point: And when he could not overcome Onias, he got him to Apollonius the governor of Coelosyria and Phenice. He ran to the other nations. They were working together on this temple, and because of one argument he goes to the other nations against Onias, and told them that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money. You cannot make this stuff up.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Jerusalem was at peace and “the laws were kept very well, because of the godliness of Onias the high priest, and his hatred of wickedness.” That is the mentality we all must have. David says it: “Ye that love the Lord, hate evil: he preserveth the souls of his saints; he delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked.”

In order for the Lord to deliver us out of the hands of the wicked, we must begin to train ourselves to hate evil. A lot of you say you hate evil, but as long as you watch pornography, you don't hate evil. As long as you watch the black woman twerking up and down, you don't hate evil. You might go on the street and say you hate evil, but at home you don't.

Onias hated wickedness, and the whole city benefited. His faith, his strength and his love for God's laws inspired everybody else, so that even the kings honored the place and magnified the temple with their best gifts, and Seleucus paid for the sacrifices out of his own revenues. Your faith helps other people's faith.

That is the promise in the psalm: the Lord preserves the souls of the saints who hate evil and delivers them from the wicked. A city led by a man who truly hates evil is kept in peace.

precepts.text: His brightness was as the light, He had horns coming out of His hand where His power was hidden, pestilence and burning coals went before Him, and He beheld and drove asunder the nations; His ways are everlasting.
precepts.point: A fire goeth before Him and burneth up His enemies round about. That is Christ coming back to destroy the nations.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
A fire goes before him and burns up his enemies round about: that is Christ coming back to destroy the nations. Habakkuk sees the same coming. “And his brightness was as the light; he had horns coming out of his hand: and there was the hiding of his power.” His power was hidden in the horns coming out of his hand.

“Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet.” That is the fire that goes before him. “He stood, and measured the earth: he beheld, and drove asunder the nations; and the everlasting mountains were scattered, the perpetual hills did bow: his ways are everlasting.” He beholds and drives the nations asunder; the fire round about is his enemies, the nations, being burned up at his return.

precepts.text: The heavens declare the glory of God; their line is gone out through all the earth, and that line is the gospel, the laws of God going out through the brothers teaching to the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: The heavens declare His righteousness and all the people see His glory. How do all the people see His glory? Israel, the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and native Indians, are His glory.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
“The heavens declare his righteousness, and all the people see his glory.” David says the same at the start of Psalm 19: “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork. Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge.”

“There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard. Their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.” That line is the gospel, the laws of God, going out through the brothers teaching to the four corners of the earth.

And how do all the people see his glory? Israel, the so-called blacks, Hispanics and native Indians, are his glory. As the line goes out, you see Israel coming back to their nationality and seeing his glory: the men are pure gold, the leaders of the earth, the kings and priests of the earth.

precepts.text: This gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness, and then the end comes; once the last person is sealed with God's laws, Christ comes back.
precepts.point: The heavens declare His righteousness and all the people see His glory. How do all the people see His glory? Israel, the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and native Indians, are His glory.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” The line gone out through all the earth in Psalm 19 is this gospel of the kingdom, preached in all the world as a witness.

Then the end comes. Once the last person is sealed with God's laws, Christ comes back, and that is when his lightnings enlighten the world, the earth sees and trembles, and the hills melt like wax at the presence of the Lord of the whole earth.

precepts.text: This is the love of God, that we keep His commandments, and His commandments are not grievous; that is how we love God.
precepts.point: He preserveth the souls of His saints and delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
Ye that love the Lord, hate evil. How do we love the Lord? We cannot hug him. “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” We love God by keeping his commandments, and they are not grievous.

If you love God's commandments you hate sin, and if you keep his commandments you abstain from breaking his laws. That is what it means to love the Lord and hate evil.

precepts.text: Good is set against evil and the godly against the sinner; God's laws are contrary to sin.
precepts.point: He preserveth the souls of His saints and delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” God's laws are contrary to sin; the two stand one against the other. “So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.”

That is why loving the Lord and hating evil go together. If you love his commandments, you are set against sin, the godly against the sinner.

precepts.text: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; that is how you preserve your soul and are delivered out of the hands of the wicked. He that despiseth His ways shall die, meaning you love evil and love sin and you will die.
precepts.point: He preserveth the souls of His saints and delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
He preserveth the souls of his saints and delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked. How? “He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; but he that despiseth his ways shall die.”

Keeping the commandment is how you preserve your soul and are delivered out of the hands of the wicked. And he that despises his ways shall die: that is loving evil and loving sin, and the end of it is death.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp and the law is light; the commandments are the light.
precepts.point: Rejoice in the Lord ye righteous, and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness. He did not forget us; He chastened us for a little but He did not forget, and He is going to remember the covenant.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
Light is sown for the righteous. What is the light? “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The commandments are the light.

That light gets sown in your mind by keeping it, and gladness comes to the upright in heart with it: loving the Lord with all our heart and soul, loving our neighbour as ourself, and bringing forth fruits of repentance like God wants us to.

precepts.text: Hear O Israel, I sow My law in you and it shall bring forth fruit; the law has to be sown in our minds, which is why we are told to study, pray, and apply.
precepts.point: Rejoice in the Lord ye righteous, and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness. He did not forget us; He chastened us for a little but He did not forget, and He is going to remember the covenant.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
Light is sown for the righteous, and the Most High says himself what he sows. “Hear me, O Israel; and mark my words, thou seed of Jacob. For, behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and ye shall be honoured in it for ever.”

The law has to be sown in our minds, and that is why we are told to study, pray and apply. Sown that way, it brings forth fruit in us: the fruits of repentance, loving the Lord and loving our neighbour. That is the gladness of the upright in heart, and we give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness because he did not forget us. He chastened us for a little, but he did not forget, and he is going to remember the covenant.
